note: Rejudged after 438bb234e4 changed handleLCPPacket: codeToEvent now reads the packet, so a Code-Reject of Codes 1-8 or a Protocol-Reject naming LCP raises RXJ- (recorded as lcpRejectFatalReason after the transition is found non-trivial), and stopRejectedCode records a rejected Echo-Request or Echo-Reply. Re-read Section 4.3's Implementation Note under RCR+/RCR- ('These events may occur on a connection which is already in the Opened state. The implementation MUST be prepared to immediately renegotiate the Configuration Options.'). Every new branch is keyed on pkt.Code == LCPCodeReject, LCPProtocolReject or ev == RXJ-, so a Configure-Request still reaches evalLCPRequest, the Opened resetAuthNegotiation and LCPDoTransition on byte-identical code and still raises RCR+/RCR-. None of the six tagged units sends a Code-Reject or Protocol-Reject as input, and all are unchanged. The server tests still require exact tld/scr/sca or tld/scr/scn actions, Ack-Sent, the Configure-Request and Ack output and no session-down; the Echo control still refuses scr/tld; the client Auth, IPCP and Network probes still require their own Configure-Request before an exact peer Ack, Identifier 0x73 and Magic 0x55667788. The verdict holds, with the earlier record caveat: the mutant records cover phase dispatch and the producer-disable records prove reachability only.
